summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue hit a 14-quarter high of Rs 1,179 crore (+12% YoY) and EBITDA Rs 172 crore (+11% YoY); management reiterates at least 20% FY27 EBITDA growth.
summary.overview: Jubilant Ingrevia reported its highest quarterly revenue and EBITDA in 14 quarters, with Q4 revenue up 12% YoY on 10% volume growth and PAT up 17% YoY to Rs 86 crore. Specialty Chemicals and Nutrition drove the quarter, while Chemical Intermediates (acetyls) benefited from inventory management as raw material prices spiked after the Middle East conflict. Net debt to EBITDA improved to 0.99x and net working capital fell to 59 days. Management guided to sequential revenue and EBITDA growth from Q1 FY27 and at least 20% full-year EBITDA growth, while flagging acetic acid prices now falling.

segments.name: Specialty Chemicals
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue Rs 516 crore (+6% YoY, +13% QoQ) with EBITDA Rs 139 crore at 27% margin, held for six quarters. Pyridine and CDMO volumes grew; CDMO revenue has grown 30-40% a year but is not disclosed separately.

segments.name: Nutrition
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue Rs 230 crore (+21% YoY, +15% QoQ) with EBITDA Rs 32 crore (+42% QoQ) at 14% margin. FY26 revenue Rs 790 crore and EBITDA Rs 100 crore; niacinamide volume led growth. Remidex Pharma acquisition completed for human nutrition premixes.

segments.name: Chemical Intermediates
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue Rs 433 crore (+15% YoY, +10% QoQ) with EBITDA improved on cost pass-through; domestic volumes rose on agro and paracetamol demand. Management expects a favourable acetic acid pricing outlook, with some inventory impact expected to clear in Q1 or early Q2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: At least 20% full-year EBITDA growth targeted for FY27; no quarterly growth guidance given.
Sequential revenue and EBITDA growth expected from Q1 FY27 onward.
Specialty Chemicals EBITDA margin sustainable at 23-25% after corporate overheads (about 25% pre-overhead); CDMO growth a positive driver.
FY27 capex of Rs 400-500 crore per year; Gajraula MPP to be completed in FY27 with production starting in Q4 FY27.
Pinnacle Journey: management says FY30 organic EBITDA targets remain achievable if pricing gains partly hold; the earlier 3x revenue and 4x EBITDA targets now depend more on organic growth.
Growth building blocks for FY27: fine chemicals, CDMO (agro, pharma, semiconductor, personal care), nutrition (organic and inorganic), and acetyls recovery.
capex_capacity: Gajraula MPP plant under construction; it is the main capex item and is expected to start production in Q4 FY27.
Bharuch CDMO plant commissioned in 14 months and capitalised in March 2026, which reduced capital WIP to about Rs 150 crore.
Pyridine and Picoline capacity of about 50,000 tonnes, running at 90%+ utilisation.
Human-grade B3 plant: PC-grade niacinamide at about 50% of estimated volumes; niacin ramp-up expected to reach 40-50% of peak volumes in FY27.
demand_pricing: Pyridine prices are at a low point while beta-picoline is at its highest level in years; management says the two offset each other. Chinese Pyridine capacity runs at 30-40% utilisation.

CDMO: the large $300 million agro contract began shipping in March 2026; FY27 volumes are still being discussed, with the customer guaranteeing make-whole volumes for any shortfall. Pipeline of 100+ opportunities worth about Rs 3,500 crore, with 20+ confirmed molecules.
New CDMO molecules ramp at about 20-25% of peak revenue in year one, 50-60% in year two and 80%+ in year three.
Acetyls: European competitors declared force majeure for a few weeks, and the company expects share gains in Europe.
Semiconductor chemicals are at an early stage with small commercial volumes and a slow customer qualification process.

qa_highlights.question: How will Chemical Intermediates spreads and inventory losses evolve after Q1 as acetyl prices fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory bought at lower prices helped Q4 and should help Q1. Any inventory loss is expected to be absorbed within Q1 or early Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company quantify quarterly and full-year EBITDA growth?
qa_highlights.answer: No quarterly guidance is given, but the company reiterates at least 20% full-year EBITDA growth, which implies a roughly linear quarterly path.

qa_highlights.question: How is the $300 million agro contract shaping FY27 volumes, and how does rupee depreciation affect it?
qa_highlights.answer: Customer has confirmed Q1 volumes; longer-term volumes are still being planned. Management says the company is naturally hedged, since its dollar import bill is about as large as its exports, so the rupee benefit will not be linear.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs 400-500 crore a year, with Gajraula MPP as the main project.

qa_highlights.question: What drives Pyridine pricing and utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Company runs about 50,000 tonnes at 90%+ utilisation. Chinese plants run at 30-40%. China Plus One demand supports the company.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable Specialty margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 23-25% after corporate overheads, which is about 25% before them; CDMO growth is a positive factor and trading cost pressure a negative.

risks_watch: Customer concentration in the large agro CDMO contract: FY27 volume scenarios are not yet firm, and the customer is under stress.
Acetyl inventory losses as acetic acid prices fall; Q1 benefit may fade in Q2.
Pharma CDMO pipeline attrition: Phase II/III molecules carry a natural mortality rate.
Pricing durability: the pricing gains that support the Pinnacle targets depend on partial retention after the Middle East disruption.
Slow semiconductor and agro qualification cycles could delay ramp-ups.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on Q4 execution and the Pinnacle Journey, but cautious and qualified on FY27 volumes, the agro customer's future schedule and the duration of acetyl benefits. Management repeatedly declined to give quarterly or contract-level numbers.
key_quotes: We will stick to our overall guidance of achieving at least 20% growth in EBITDA through the year.

So we are hopeful that whatever inventory impact has to come, we will be able to nullify within this quarter or at best in the early part of next quarter and hence, minimize any negative impact coming from that in Q2.
We are fully covered and we will go as per the projections that we have committed to the markets in terms of bottom line.
Pyridine is an old molecule, and we are global leaders in that.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 5 per share (final Rs 2.5), cash outflow Rs 79.8 crore

adds.what: Bharuch CDMO plant (commissioned and capitalised March 2026)

growth.why: Management reiterates at least 20% FY27 EBITDA growth and sequential revenue/EBITDA growth from Q1 FY27, backed by a $300m agro CDMO contract (visibility only for Q1), a Rs 3,500 crore CDMO pipeline with 20+ confirmed molecules, and Gajraula MPP starting Q4 FY27, but no quarterly growth guidance and no full-year volume numbers.
